replies.author: @Gabe1248-x8u
replies.text:
​​@SocratesAth Denmark doesn't really consume whatever electricity they produce. The problem with intermittent energy sources like wind is that you usually either produce too little or too much of it. When they produce too much of it they sell most of abroad and when they produce too little they import. So in the end the Danish consumer is going to use foreign produced electricity rather than their own despite on the big whole they might produce about as much as they consume but doesn't really mean they actually use their own. 

Only reason Denmark can even do this is because countries like Sweden and Norway has stable base powers like hydro and nuclear plants which makes it possible for them to import when the wind is not blowing.
